status: first-person swamp concept proposal; not playable
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept / camera transformation.
Make a FIRST-PERSON WALK-THROUGH SWAMP TUNNEL version of reference image 1, the swamp game concept. Reference 2 shows the game's first-person portrait/math layout; borrow ONLY its camera/layout logic, not stone architecture or the closed door. Transform the side-view swamp into a close, tangible corridor of gnarled willow trunks, arching roots and hanging moss, as if the player is walking INTO that same printed illustration. Preserve its EXACT irregular black medieval woodcut linework, natural light parchment, dirty-orange accents and shabby absurd dark-fantasy character design.

Wide 16:9 single game-screen concept. The upper 73 percent is the swamp corridor. Broad muddy walking ground and a few sunken uneven wooden planks lead from the bottom foreground into the middle distance, with black still-water channels and carved pale ripples on both sides. Large twisted trees rise on the left and right; their branches interlock overhead into irregular open arches. Repeated receding tree/root surrounds at three depths, subtly staggered left and right so the passage feels like it winds through the swamp. Each surround has a large clear central opening. Keep a generous traversable route, not a tiny hole or wall of roots. No flat far-end wall, no closed door, no stone dungeon, no tiled paving. Far passage curves into pitch-black ink undergrowth. The nearest bark and mud have clear pale paper interiors and crisp carved detail, farther trunks increasingly absorbed into dark ink so a light carried by the viewer is implied. Darkness made with solid ink and hatching; no digital lighting gradients or fog overlays. Sparse pale blank space around the nearby encounter keeps it readable.

An angry, squat, broad, warty toad from reference 1, still wearing its stupid dented cooking-pot helmet, faces directly toward the camera on the path, full silhouette, medium distance, strong enough foreground contrast to be readable. Make it threatening but absurd. Behind it, off to one side farther along the bend, the thin ragged bog revenant with its rusty pole-blade is only a partly revealed silhouette emerging from blackness. Tiny pale eye glints in SMALL shaded sockets, never large staring white eyeballs, laser eyes or empty demon holes. The toad blocks the route but not the whole picture. Reed clumps, mushrooms, complete roots and a couple of partly submerged old shields at the margins; no busy prop carpet. No gore or faces growing on trees or bodies.

Near the bottom of the world scene, the same compact row of FOUR inset portrait frames as reference 2: bucket-helmet knight with visor down; orange-hooded priest; strange human wizard in black hat with tiny eye glints; chainmail-coif firestarter. Each has two small hearts. They are HUD portraits, not physical characters standing on the path. Keep them modest, with the corridor the dominant image. Below: ONE thin worn black divider/timing line, orange central diamond, a small shield near quarter, a small flaming sword at halfway, small plain sword at three quarters and stick near the right end; a modest orange fill along the left. Under the line a pale parchment maths area with the large carved equation exactly "9 + 6 = ?" matching reference 1's lettering. No extra labels, captions, title, cards, buttons or sound-effect text.

Woodblock and engraved print, not a painting. Dense fine hatching on monsters; deliberate air between environmental lines. The same parchment palette as the side-scrolling swamp, charcoal ink and light warm paper, muted earth shades and very limited dirty orange. No green/yellow screen tint, no blue/purple, no glowing effects, no glossy wet surfaces, no photorealism, no 3D, no pixel art, no modern cartoon simplification. This should look like the same old illustrated book suddenly gains depth. One immersive scene, not a sprite sheet, diagram or montage.
